dedupe_keys.name: celestrak socrates plus satellite orbital conjunction reports assessing threatening encounters in space

description: SOCRATES Plus publishes conjunction reports that screen active satellites against the full catalogue of Earth-orbiting objects and rank close approaches, listing for each pair the time of closest approach, minimum distance and maximum collision probability. CelesTrak, run by T.S. Kelso, has offered SOCRATES since 2004 as a free public service; SOCRATES Plus, introduced in 2023, screens only active payloads (7,292 of 10,154 payloads were considered active in March 2023) and skips pairs within the same constellation. Screening uses STK/CAT on public general perturbations data and reports all conjunctions within 5 km, with the maximum probability method (after Alfano) preferred over minimum distance. Coverage is all catalogued objects in Earth orbit. Format and access: top 10 lists, a search interface and report files documented on the site, without login. Licence: not stated on the page; free. Caveats: general perturbations data lack covariance, so probabilities are approximate and conservative. It supports hazard exposure analysis of collision risk to satellite infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the CelesTrak GP and SATCAT data it screens and the TraCSS conjunction assessment verification dataset.
